title: Record the Stage B rulings: subscription pays, 7-day limit governs, calibration stays at 12
body:
Three owner rulings, given in chat before Stage B's plan is written, appended to `docs/DECISIONS.md`. No code.

The file's own header: *"ADR-lite. One dated entry per decision ... A recorded ruling is never silently reversed."* And `AGENTS.md`'s standing rule that chat is not storage. These settle three questions **BL-23** and **OD-22** leave open, which a planner would otherwise guess at.

**1. The subscription pays**, via `claude -p`. The API was rejected for a specific reason rather than on cost: **R26 caps spend at 10% of the weekly SUBSCRIPTION limits, and an API call never moves that meter.** The guard would read the same percentage before, during and after every batch and report healthy while a card was charged without limit — a gate watching a dial its own run is not connected to. The subscription path is also the only one where R8's token counts and R26's points readings come from the same run.

**2. `Weekly (7-day)` governs**, the account-wide limit, not the model-scoped one beside it. It comes from Anthropic's own usage endpoint, so it counts every session on the subscription — other machines, web sessions and spawned workers included, which is the property that makes the cap meaningful.

**3. Calibration stays at 12 bundles.** The token comparison R8 requires is exact at any size. The points difference is not — the reader returns whole percentages, so a batch eating under one percent reads identically before and after. The plan will record a zero delta as what it is, unmeasurable at this size, rather than enlarging the batch to force a reading it does not need.

None of the three requires a design edit. R26 already names the reader and the figure; R8 as amended on 2026-08-25 (#185) already requires the two quantities kept apart and every estimate stored with its assumptions.

This lands **before** the Stage B plan, not with it — the ordering rule ESC-18 and ESC-20 record. The plan will cite this entry, and a citation to an unlanded entry is false at the only moment anything checks it.

Ran locally against this diff: `plan-resolve.sh`, `escape-refs.sh`.
